title: What is keeping this market alive?

observed_trades.setup: One of his best-acting winners; refuses to let go of it while struggling elsewhere.
observed_trades.quote: AMD is not doing anything wrong. I just can't uh get rid of it.

observed_trades.setup: Cyber leader held as a winner; not easy to get repositioned up here.
observed_trades.quote: Strikes another Octa's one that I own and and okay fine
observed_trades.notes: He adds 'You had to have bought them a few weeks ago when I did' (05:03) - an undated earlier entry, not logged as a separate row.

observed_trades.setup: Core IBIT shares from mid-August, held while above the 200 simple moving average.
observed_trades.stop: hold so long as it lives above the 200 simple moving average
observed_trades.quote: keep the rest of my shares that I bought from middle of August
observed_trades.notes: Ticker named at 15:15 ('add to my IBIT one time') and 01:11 ('High bit ... I just won't get rid of it').

observed_trades.setup: Single add to the IBIT winner.
observed_trades.stop: would trim the rest of the add on a loss of Monday's low and the 20 simple moving average
observed_trades.quote: Um I I did add some shares on the 17th.
observed_trades.notes: Ticker named at 15:15 ('I've had the ability to add to my IBIT one time').

observed_trades.setup: Trimmed part of the shares added on the 17th; trailing the rest.
observed_trades.quote: I did trim some off. I would likely trim off the rest of those
observed_trades.notes: Trim date not given (after the 17th). 'Those' = the added shares.

observed_trades.setup: Short gold miners, working; wishes it were bigger and that he had more shorts on.
observed_trades.quote: I do have some GDX. I do not have enough GDX.
observed_trades.notes: Short side stated at 01:22: 'GDX continues to fade on the short side. Now, mind you, um I I do wish I had a couple more shorts on'.

observed_trades.setup: Mean-reversion snapback attempt in small caps (rate-sensitive, crowded short).
observed_trades.quote: I like the idea of trying to play TNA for a snapback or the IWM. Um and I had a position today
observed_trades.notes: Instrument not specified - 'TNA ... or the IWM'; vehicle left null. Long side implied by 'snapback'.

observed_trades.quote: I had a position today but just not strong enough to want to keep.
observed_trades.notes: Instrument not specified (TNA or IWM); vehicle left null.

observed_trades.setup: Low-risk pullback into an ascending moving average: morning wash, VWAP reclaim; then did nothing the rest of the day.
observed_trades.entry_basis: VWAP reclaim after a morning wash
observed_trades.quote: But Dell, you know, I I saw the morning wash. I got the reclaim of VWAP. I got long a little bit
observed_trades.notes: 'today I wanted to get long something' in the preceding sentence (05:14). He passed on the same setup in MRVL because he had already bought Dell.

observed_trades.setup: Did nothing after the entry; no cushion to hold overnight.
observed_trades.quote: Again, I buy Dell, it doesn't work. I don't buy Marvel.
observed_trades.notes: Exit not said in so many words: 'I buy Dell, it doesn't work', and he says he will not force a hold when the stock gives no cushion (19:42-20:01). Logged per the failed-attempt convention.

observed_trades.setup: Morning washout, undercut of a prior day low, VWAP reclaim.
observed_trades.entry_basis: VWAP reclaim after a morning washout / undercut of the prior day low
observed_trades.quote: Intel I bought yesterday, but what happened with Intel?
observed_trades.notes: It took off from the open today without him ('I was in this thing four dollars ago').

observed_trades.setup: Did not close well; sold for a small loss rather than hold red overnight.
observed_trades.quote: Intel doesn't close well. I let it go and I don't take a big loss on it
observed_trades.notes: 'yesterday' is two sentences earlier in the same passage (18:30).

observed_trades.setup: Felt like a good entry; gave it back on Friday, then it turned back up without him.
observed_trades.quote: just like PNW a few days ago. you know, you feel like you get yourself a pretty good entry uh right in here
observed_trades.notes: Second-person narration anchored by the preceding first-person sentence 'The market hasn't rewarded me for putting positions on' (08:59). Entry date not pinned (before Friday 2026-09-25).

observed_trades.setup: Gave the trade back on Friday's cyber sell-off; bullish engulfing Monday and breakout today came after.
observed_trades.quote: and then all of a sudden on Friday you're giving it back up
observed_trades.notes: Second person; 'giving it back up' read as being out of the trade (he presents it as an example of how hard it is to get positioned). Not an explicit exit statement.
